human_authorization: User explicitly requested review and closure of all nine supplied findings; canonical promotion remains a separate human act after full propagation/verification.

deltas.title: Bootstrap trust root for first accepted DesignEpoch
deltas.change: Define a BootstrapTrustRootCeremony profile over the existing TrustRootCeremonyReceipt and add FrozenVerifierBinding. The first accepted DesignEpoch must bind a content-addressed ceremony transcript, named independent verifier implementations/checker roots, immutable test corpus/root, participants/witnesses/authority and explicit bootstrap scope. Before this receipt passes, a source may be SPECIFIED_DESIGNEPOCH_CANDIDATE but not ACCEPTED.
deltas.do_nothing: Leaving bootstrap independence implicit permits the first verifier trust root to be selected without a machine-checkable non-self-verification ceremony; this is incompatible with P24/GSL-SELF-009 at the initial epoch boundary.

deltas.title: Shared-state-mediated authority composition
deltas.change: Action-eligible Claims/artifacts carry an AuthorityProvenanceChain. If actor B executes action a because of artifact x produced/authorized through principal/agent A, effective authority is intersection(B action authority, every controlling authority in x.authority_provenance). Shared-state handoff is an authority composition edge, not an authority reset. Empty intersection rejects execution.
deltas.do_nothing: MAC-001 states the non-amplification property but does not currently make knowledge-mediated causal reachability an explicit authority-composition input, leaving implementation latitude for A-write/B-act amplification.

deltas.title: Deterministic let binding grammar
deltas.change: Replace optional-expression LetExpr ambiguity with LetExpr ::= let Pattern (: Type)? = Expr in Expr and introduce LetStmt ::= let Pattern (: Type)? = Expr ;?. LetStmt is valid only in BlockExpr/module statement scope, introduces a lexical binding in that enclosing scope and has Unit result; a bare let is no longer parsed as an expression.
deltas.do_nothing: The current optional 'in Expr' permits a complete expression with no specified result/scope and forces compilers to invent semantics.

deltas.title: Deterministic QueryStmt result semantics
deltas.change: QueryStmt resolves a QueryResultBinding. `query Expr into ID` binds the typed query result to ID in the enclosing lexical scope. A query without `into` must target a declared module/process output sink in the active FunctionContract; otherwise compilation fails QUERY_RESULT_UNCONSUMED. Query does not implicitly mutate Knowledge or create Evidence.
deltas.do_nothing: Current grammar admits a result without specifying destination, scope or distinction from eval, defeating deterministic compilation and FunctionContract closure.

deltas.title: Causal-level-qualified causes relation
deltas.change: The existing Core Relation `causes` remains one relation identity but every operational causes edge carries CausalRelationLevelBinding(level:C0..C4, model/assumption/evidence/identification refs as applicable). Consumers declare a minimum causal level; consuming a lower-level edge as a stronger level returns CAUSAL_LEVEL_UNDERFLOW. C2+ requires a declared causal/mechanistic model; C3/C4 additionally require the applicable intervention/counterfactual identification obligations.
deltas.do_nothing: Existing non-amplification rules protect causal Claims but the raw relation type does not itself prevent a C0/C1 edge from being consumed as C2+ by an implementation.

deltas.title: R0 Sanity Gate separated from Reason modes
deltas.change: R0 remains the historical assurance-depth label for transition sanity but is typed as SanityGate, a terminating deterministic/total predicate over available transition type/scope/abstraction/obvious contradiction inputs with PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN. Engine.Reason modes are R1..R4. Invoking R1..R4 may require SanityGate first; SanityGate does not recursively invoke Engine.Reason, closing the self-reference at the minimum tier.
deltas.do_nothing: Calling R0 a Reason tier while Reason is logically present at every meaningful transition leaves a semantic self-reference whose practical TerminationContract does not define the base case.

deltas.title: Rights registry ordering clarification
deltas.change: Generated/readable rights views order active RIGHT-001..025 first and then explicit non-active RIGHT-026 RESERVED and RIGHT-027 ON_HOLD. Canonical identifiers and definitions do not change. Add a note that identifier order is not semantic and reserved/on-hold slots may remain historically interleaved in immutable source history.
deltas.do_nothing: Current owner text is semantically clear but the 026/027-before-024/025 layout is unnecessarily confusing to human readers and generated views.

deltas.title: Committed provenance class manifest distinguishes redaction from absence
deltas.change: High-assurance provenance views carry a ProvenanceClassManifest committed by Merkle/content root. The manifest declares expected node classes and edge kinds without exposing protected payloads. For an authorized view, an expected-but-undisclosed class is REDACTED/PROTECTED with a commitment; an expected class with no valid committed node/edge is PROVENANCE_GAP; a class outside the declared applicable manifest is NOT_APPLICABLE. Redaction metadata remains privacy-minimized.
deltas.do_nothing: PROV-005 requires protected gaps to be declared but the returned lineage view lacks a machine-checkable way to distinguish redaction from true absence without inspecting hidden graph state.

deltas.title: Catalogue closure for AuthorityDecl and EffectDecl
deltas.change: Register AuthorityDecl and EffectDecl as FOUNDATIONAL_CONTRACT catalogue entries with stable SchemaIDs and generated machine layouts. Their grammar productions remain unchanged. This avoids inventing a second semantic identity or folding away useful explicit declarations.
deltas.do_nothing: The grammar exposes machine-facing declaration forms whose catalogue/schema targets are not independently resolvable, leaving a type/reference-closure gap.
